title: John Leguizamo Reveals The Odyssey's Secret Script Process
excerpt:
Christopher Nolan's assistant personally delivered the screenplay.
Script revisions required Leguizamo to return the old pages.
body_md:
John Leguizamo, who plays Eumaeus in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, has described the unusual process of receiving the film's screenplay. Before obtaining the script, he did not know the full extent of his role.

One of Nolan's personal assistants delivered the screenplay directly to the actor. The precautions continued throughout revisions: whenever Nolan changed the script, Leguizamo had to surrender the superseded pages.

The procedure was unlike anything the actor had previously experienced. Although the movie adapts Homer's familiar epic, the filmmakers sought to protect the particulars of their interpretation and execution. The available interview extract does not reproduce every detail of the handover.

Leguizamo considered the experience worthwhile, and his performance as Eumaeus drew critical praise. His account illustrates Nolan's attention to controlling screenplay circulation throughout a major production.
